A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VAMBA research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across layout and section-number changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original component and distillation ablations, video-understanding evaluations, efficiency measurements and qualitative examples in Tables 2–5 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds a token-reduction experiment reporting GPU memory and benchmark scores in Table 6.

M1.justification: Appendix Section 10 introduces VAMBA-TR, an inference variant that uniformly drops 50% of video tokens. The core Mamba-2/cross-attention architecture, initialization strategy, losses and two-stage training procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Evaluation coverage is unchanged; Table 6 reuses LVBench, Video-MME and MLVU. However, Section 4.2 replaces the named full-scale training sources with an unspecified approximately 7M image/video QA collection. The PDFs do not establish whether the underlying training-data coverage changed or only its description was shortened.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the established benchmark, efficiency and qualitative comparisons are unchanged. STORM and BIMBA are newly discussed but not experimentally evaluated; Table 6 adds an internal token-reduction ablation of VAMBA.

E3.justification: Section 10 adds evaluation with full tokens versus uniformly dropping 50% during inference on three existing benchmarks. Existing splits, metrics and ablation settings are retained. The newly stated approximately 7M training total does not establish an increased training budget.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds a single-rate token-reduction experiment testing compatibility and the memory–accuracy tradeoff. The component and distillation ablations, efficiency analyses and qualitative examples in Figures 5–6 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals or significance tests for the reported experiments. The new Table 6 likewise reports point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing results remain unchanged. New Table 6 reports VAMBA/VAMBA-TR memory of 45,791/33,847 MB and scores of 42.4/41.6 on LVBench, 57.4/56.9 on Video-MME and 65.9/66.5 on MLVU. These are additional results: its VAMBA scores differ from the retained main-table values of 42.1 and 57.8 without explaining the settings difference.

T1.justification: The state-space definitions, attention and Mamba equations, training-loss formulations and complexity reasoning in Sections 2–3 and Table 1 are unchanged. The appendix additions introduce no formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about efficient hour-long video understanding, the hybrid architecture, frame capacity and benchmark advantage. The additional token-reduction evidence does not redefine those main claims.

C2.justification: Section 10 extends the earlier general suggestion of combining VAMBA with token reduction by interpreting the experiment as preserving most capability and proposing finetuning with reduction to better preserve performance. Section 9 also adds an architectural explanation for differences from STORM and BIMBA.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 adds an approximately 7M instruction-data total but removes the explicit full-scale source list and the 2M LLaVA-OneVision component count; Appendix 7 does not restore them. The introduction corrects A100 to A800, matching existing implementation details. Section 10 documents the new 50% inference-token dropping rule.

R1.justification: New Appendix Section 9 cites STORM and BIMBA and distinguishes their compression modules from VAMBA's decoder-level architectural changes. ActivityNet-QA and Perception Test references disappear with the shortened training-data description. The broader related-work positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order remain unchanged. V2 shortens the training-data description and several related-work sentences, updates affiliation/contact text, and inserts two appendix sections, renumbering Additional Qualitative Results from Section 9 to Section 11.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 6, reduces Figure 2's displayed size and adjusts spacing and page flow. Existing tables and figures retain their scientific contents, including Figure 6; its accompanying discussion moves to the following appendix page.

improvement.justification: The token-reduction experiment and comparison with STORM/BIMBA add useful evidence and context. However, v2 removes explicit full-scale training-data provenance, while Table 6 introduces unexplained baseline-score differences and gives limited experimental settings. These benefits coexist with reduced reproducibility and unresolved interpretation of the new results, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
